tasks.title: OpenRouter dynamic model search & switching in Agent Chat
tasks.description: Extend the shipped fixed-allowlist OpenRouter provider (openrouter-gpt-latest) with a live, searchable catalog: the user can search OpenRouter's full model list and switch to any of them per turn, with per-model reasoning-effort options. Confirmed direction: fully open catalog, live API-backed (not a curated static list). Full design record: docs/OPENROUTER-DYNAMIC-MODELS-PLAN.md.
tasks.details: Reverses subtask 1.1's "no dynamic catalog fetching" non-goal — justified because this app is single-user (one GATEWAY_AUTH_USER, one OPENROUTER_API_KEY owned by that same user), so "any model reachable" collapses to "the key's owner reaches any model with their own key," not a multi-tenant exposure. AgentModelSchema stays a CLOSED enum (do not widen it — composer.tsx's MODEL_LABELS/MODEL_PROVIDER Records and modelSupportsEffort() are exhaustive over it); openrouter-gpt-latest is repurposed as the "OpenRouter provider slot" and a new optional AgentUserMessageSchema field `openrouterModelId` selects a specific catalog entry per turn, validated server-side against a freshly-fetched catalog before ever reaching the upstream request body. Catalog comes from GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (data[].{id,name,context_length,pricing.{prompt,completion},reasoning.{supported_efforts,mandatory}} — reasoning.supported_efforts uses the SAME vocabulary as AgentReasoningEffortSchema, verified live this session). Delivered over a new WS request/response frame pair on the existing authenticated /agent socket (NOT a new REST endpoint — avoids duplicating the WS upgrade's origin+cookie auth story), server-side cached with a TTL and stale-on-fetch-failure fallback. See docs/OPENROUTER-DYNAMIC-MODELS-PLAN.md for the full grounding, schema diff, and rationale — read it before starting any subtask.

Acceptance for the whole task: full existing suites (agent-service test+typecheck, terminal typecheck) stay green throughout, and the base fixed-model OpenRouter provider (already shipped) keeps working unchanged when openrouterModelId is omitted.

subtasks.title: Build the OpenRouter catalog fetch/cache module + WS delivery
subtasks.description: agent-service fetches, reduces, and caches OpenRouter's live model list, and serves it over the existing authenticated /agent WS socket.
subtasks.details:
New apps/agent-service/src/openrouter-catalog.ts: fetch GET `${config.openrouter.baseUrl}/models` (send the configured Authorization header even though OpenRouter doesn't require it, for consistency), reduce the raw `data[]` to the OpenRouterCatalogModelSchema shape from 3.1 (id, name, context_length->contextLength, pricing.prompt/completion, reasoning.supported_efforts->supportedEfforts + reasoning.mandatory when the `reasoning` key is present, else omit the reasoning field entirely). In-memory cache, TTL default 10 min via new `OPENROUTER_CATALOG_TTL_MS` config (config.ts, optional()), refreshed lazily past TTL; on a refetch failure, serve the last-known-good cached list (log, never throw) — an empty/never-fetched cache does one bounded synchronous fetch (~5s timeout) before replying. In apps/agent-service/src/index.ts (or agent-loop.ts, wherever WS client messages are dispatched), handle the new `openrouter_models_request` frame: reply `openrouter_models_response` with the cached list (empty list + no fetch attempt when `config.openrouter.apiKey` is unset — mirrors the existing "hidden unless configured" rule). Acceptance/tests: a new openrouter-catalog.test.ts against a local mock HTTP server (same pattern as agent-loop-openrouter.test.ts) covering fetch->reduce, TTL expiry triggering a refetch, and stale-serve on a failing refetch; a WS-level test proving the request/response round trip and the empty-when-unconfigured case.

subtasks.title: Wire the per-turn catalog id into resolveModel and the streaming loop
subtasks.description: A turn carrying openrouterModelId routes to that exact upstream model, validated server-side against the cached catalog; reasoning-effort support becomes per-model instead of a fixed provider-wide flag.
subtasks.details:
apps/agent-service/src/azure.ts: extend resolveModel's "openrouter-gpt-latest" branch to accept an optional catalog id argument. When provided: look it up in the cached catalog (from 3.2) — a hit sets `deployment` to that id and `supportsReasoningEffort` to whether the catalog entry has a `reasoning` field (mirrors the schema's optional reasoning block); a miss returns undefined (surfaces the existing "model not configured" error frame — never forward an unvalidated id upstream). When omitted, behavior is UNCHANGED (falls back to config.openrouter.model, supportsReasoningEffort: false) — this is the backward-compat guarantee for every already-shipped/persisted turn. agent-loop.ts: thread `openrouterModelId` from the parsed AgentUserMessage through to handleUserMessage/resolveModel's call site; when the resolved model supports reasoning but the specific model's `reasoning.mandatory` is true and requested effort is \"none\", either upgrade to the catalog's `default_effort` or reject with a clear error (pick one and document it in the AGENT-PROTOCOL.md update in 3.6 — do not silently send \"none\" to a model that requires reasoning). Acceptance/tests: resolveModel unit tests for hit/miss/omitted-id cases including the mandatory-reasoning edge case; extend agent-loop-openrouter.test.ts (or add a sibling) proving a turn with a valid openrouterModelId sends that exact id as `model` in the outgoing request body, and an invalid id never reaches the mock server at all (surfaces the error frame instead). Full existing agent-service suite must stay green (this touches a function every current OpenRouter test already exercises).
